blocks.text: The argument for school cellphone bans is simple: Phones offer endless distraction. Take them away and students can focus on classwork, engage with peers and, ultimately, learn more. But the reality is more complicated, as emerging research shows. Schools can lock phones away in pouches or banish them to backpacks, but they can’t shut out the digital world. In the past few years, more than 40 U.S. states have passed laws that restrict cellphones at schools, according to the Phone Free Schools State Report Card, which tracks state phone legislation.
